title: Business Continuity Planning (BCP)
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 1: Security and Risk Management: Business Continuity Planning (BCP).

items: BIA identifies critical business functions and the impact of disruption
Determines maximum tolerable downtime for each function
Identifies dependencies between business functions
Prioritizes recovery efforts based on criticality
Must have senior management support and sponsorship

blocks.text: The BIA is the first step in BCP. It identifies and prioritizes critical business functions and determines the impact of disruption to each. BIA output includes:

items: List of critical business functions ranked by priority
Maximum tolerable downtime for each function
Resource requirements for recovery
Dependencies between functions
Financial and operational impact estimates

blocks.text: From Destination CISSP: "If your team is not truly representative of the organization, you may miss critical priorities. Be sure to gather input from all parts of the organization." From Shon Harris: "The BCP coordinator would need to implement specific requirements to ensure that the defined objectives within the scope can be accomplished."

items: RPO (Recovery Point Objective) — Maximum acceptable data loss measured in time
RTO (Recovery Time Objective) — Maximum time to restore service after disruption
WRT (Work Recovery Time) — Time to verify system integrity after restoration
MTD (Maximum Tolerable Downtime) — Total time a process can be disrupted
MTD = RTO + WRT

rows: RTO = 2 hours → must be up within 2 hours

items: RPO determines backup frequency (shorter RPO = more frequent backups)
RTO determines recovery site type (shorter RTO = hotter site)
MTD is the business-driven constraint that determines RTO and WRT
RTO + WRT must not exceed MTD

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: MTD = RTO + WRT. If the MTD is 4 hours and RTO is 2 hours, the WRT is 2 hours. The exam tests this arithmetic. ⚠️ Exam Trap: RPO is about DATA LOSS, not downtime. RTO is about SERVICE RESTORATION. They are independent metrics.

items: Project Scope and Planning — Define scope, get management support
Business Impact Analysis (BIA) — Identify critical functions and impacts
Continuity Planning — Develop strategies and procedures
Approval and Implementation — Get management sign-off, implement plan
Testing and Exercises — Validate the plan works
Maintenance — Keep the plan updated

blocks.text: Senior Management Support is CRITICAL: From Chapple: "When working on a business continuity plan, the BCP team's executive acknowledged the importance of his support and agreed to participate. He sent an email to all employees introducing the effort and stating that it had his full backing." The BCP must be a living document — updated whenever the organization changes:

items: New systems or applications
Personnel changes
Business process changes
After every test/exercise
After any actual disaster

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: Senior management support is the MOST CRITICAL success factor for BCP. Without it, the plan will fail.

From Destination CISSP: "A cold site is basically just a shell of a building that needs to be populated with equipment, data, and people. It usually takes weeks to bring a cold site online. The biggest advantage of a cold site is cost — it's cheap." "A warm site is better than a cold site, because in addition to the shell of a building, basic equipment is available and perhaps partially configured." From Chapple: "Activation of a warm site typically takes at least 12 hours from the time a disaster is declared. This does not mean that any site that can be activated in less than 12 hours qualifies as a hot site, however; switchover times for most hot sites are often measured in seconds or minutes." Reciprocal Agreements: From Chapple: Organizations may enter agreements to share their facilities. However, these are unreliable because:

items: Both organizations may be affected by the same disaster
Sharing resources may compromise security
Capacity may be insufficient for both organizations

blocks.text: From Destination CISSP: "Another method of reducing the expense of a hot site is to use the hot site as a development or testing environment during normal operations." ⚠️ Exam Trap: Hot site = fastest activation, highest cost. Cold site = slowest activation, lowest cost. Warm site = middle ground. The exam loves trade-off questions about cost vs. recovery time.

items: Checklist Test — Review the plan on paper (least disruptive)
Structured Walk-through (Tabletop) — Team discusses scenarios around a table
Simulation Test — Practice specific scenarios without affecting operations
Parallel Test — Activate alternate site while primary remains operational
Full Interruption Test — Shut down primary, operate from alternate (most disruptive)

blocks.text: Tests should progress from least to most disruptive. Never start with a full interruption test. ⚠️ Exam Trap: A parallel test runs the alternate site alongside the primary — both are operational simultaneously. A full interruption test actually shuts down the primary. The exam distinguishes between these.
